column3: The Hebrew uses “many days” and the image of entering into days for advanced age; BSB has “A long time” and “well along in years.”
The Hebrew explicitly names Joshua again and says he has “entered into days”; BSB uses “he” and “well along in years.”
The Hebrew says “the going in of the sun”; BSB expresses the direction as “westward.”
The Hebrew has singular “the name” of their gods and uses a causative verb for making an oath; BSB has plural “names” and “swear.”
The Hebrew says one man will “pursue” a thousand; BSB says he “can put a thousand to flight.”
The Hebrew explicitly names “your souls”; BSB says “yourselves.”
The Hebrew ends with a reciprocal statement, “you go in to them, and they to you”; BSB combines this as associating with them.
The Hebrew twice says no word has “fallen” and says all have “come”; BSB uses “failed” and the passive “was fulfilled.”

The Hebrew repeats the speaking root for the good word and says “all the evil word”; BSB has “promised” and expands the latter to “the calamity He has threatened.” The Hebrew also explicitly names “the LORD your God” at the end, where BSB uses “He.”
